newsitem.title: USA: US Treasuries, pounded by profit-taking, end down.
newsitem.headline: US Treasuries, pounded by profit-taking, end down.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries took it on the chin Thursday, plunging to levels not seen in almost a month, as big accounts continued to book profits ahead of Friday's November jobs report.
The 30-year bond closed at 99-28/32, down 1-1/2 points from Wednesday. Its yield jumped to 6.51 percent -- a level not seen since its Novemeber 8 close -- up from 6.40 percent.
"We have probably seen the highs for the time being," said Jim Kenney, head trader at Prudential Securities.
Market participants said the selloff was technically driven, with large accounts taking profits after the big rally the past few months.

"People who have money walked out with the long bond at 6.39 percent. They said, 'am I willing to hold (these levels) through employment, PPI, CPI and retail sales?'" Kenney said, noting that the answer was "no." "That's why they took a hike."
Friday, the Labor Department releases its November employment report, with the market looking for a 179,000 rise in nonfarm payrolls.
